event.name: QCon San Francisco 2026
event.notes: video_expected: false = schedule shows 'No Video Available'; true = conference keynote/talk with no such label (inferred, not confirmed); null = training or unknown. Abstracts and bios are paraphrased summaries, not quotes.

tracks.name: Architectures You've Always Wondered About
tracks.description: Real-world architectures from well-known systems, with the trade-offs and design decisions behind them.

tracks.name: Guardrails & Safety Nets (Evals) for the New Landscape
tracks.description: How teams build evals, feedback loops and safety mechanisms that make AI-powered systems reliable and trustworthy.

tracks.name: Modern API Design for Humans and Agents
tracks.description: Designing APIs that both human developers and AI agents can discover, use safely and recover with: contracts, protocols, retries, partial failure, evolving domain models.

tracks.name: Resilience Engineering: Everything Fails All the Time
tracks.description: Designing systems and organizations that expect failure, adapt to it and keep operating under stress.

tracks.name: Distributed Systems in Production
tracks.description: Practitioner lessons on latency, consistency models, sharding, multi-region, incidents and observability; trade-offs over idealized designs.

tracks.name: Engineering AI Systems
tracks.description: Taking AI past the prototype: reliability, evaluation, infrastructure, autonomous workflows, regulated domains and inference at scale.

tracks.name: Staff+ Engineering Skills
tracks.description: How Staff+ ICs lead orgs through technical transitions (cloud, monolith breakups, AI adoption): growing peers, cross-team leadership, owning ambiguity.

tracks.name: Data Platforms Reimagined
tracks.description: How data platforms are changing for real-time, AI-driven and decentralized workloads, and how that reshapes data flow in organizations.

tracks.name: Architecting for Agents: Beneath the Loop
tracks.description: The layers under the agent loop: model portability, durable state, deployment, sandboxed execution and observability, from people running agents in production.

tracks.name: Engineering the Developer Experience
tracks.description: DevEx as a deliberate discipline in the AI era: productivity measurement, build/tooling as architecture, agent workflows, platforms for humans and agents, culture and skills.

tracks.name: Real World Platform Engineering
tracks.description: How orgs build internal platforms for faster delivery, safer ops and lower cognitive load, balancing standardization and flexibility at scale.

tracks.name: Code Beyond Engineers & Engineering Teams
tracks.description: Coding is spreading beyond engineers into product, ops and AI-assisted roles; what that means for teams, ownership and systems.

sessions.title: The Harness Is the New Operating System
sessions.abstract: Agents generate behavior at runtime, so a 'harness' layer is needed to make it dependable, much as OSes abstracted hardware. Builds a first-principles model of harnesses using coding agents, mapping OS concerns (processes, memory, I/O, protection, observability) onto agents.

sessions.title: Learning Out Loud (Under Near-Existential Pressure)
sessions.abstract: Developers must master constantly shifting tools while shipping into old, bug-laden codebases. A former teacher turned Photoshop engineer uses research on how people learn to suggest lowering the stakes of failure and trading an expert identity for a learner one.

sessions.title: The Execution Muscle: Why Great Teams Are Built, Not Hired
sessions.abstract: Stalled teams usually suffer from daily habits, not talent, tools or process. Execution is a trainable skill; covers three habits: building trust, sharing ownership, and making expectations and feedback routine.

sessions.title: Game Time: How to (Unsuccessfully) 10x in a Week & (Successfully) 10x in a Year
sessions.abstract: A telehealth team hit overnight demand it wasn't built for and fumbled a one-week scale-up. Lessons on scaling a live system: metrics, milestones, why more time alone doesn't help, and letting go of existing patterns.

sessions.title: Live Resharding Without Regret: Lessons from Building Valkey's Atomic Slot Migration
sessions.abstract: Moving gigabytes of state between live nodes under heavy load without dropping keys, blocking the event loop or breaking client abstractions: lessons from building Valkey's atomic slot migration.

sessions.title: Architecting Nubank's Global Financial Infrastructure
sessions.abstract: Brazil's Pix instant payments (130M+ customers) demand no maintenance downtime, strong consistency and controlled cloud cost. Covers Nubank's runtimes, database design, zero-downtime techniques and the technical/organizational trade-offs behind rapid growth under regulation.

sessions.title: How to Build a Real-Time Voice Agent
sessions.abstract: A voice agent is more than a chatbot with a microphone; walks through what it takes to build one that responds in real time (only a short teaser is published).

sessions.title: Inside the Disaggregated Architecture Serving LLM Inference
sessions.abstract: LLM requests have a compute-bound prefill phase and a memory-bandwidth-bound decode phase. Explains serving them on separate, specialized hardware rather than one shared system.

sessions.title: Generation Got Cheap, Trust Didn't: Scaling Agentic Changes from Prompt to Prod at Roblox
sessions.abstract: As agents write more of Roblox's production code, the bottleneck shifts from producing changes to deciding which to trust. How Roblox moves agent-generated changes from prompt to production at scale.

sessions.title: Unconference: Architectures You've Always Wondered About
sessions.abstract: Open-space discussion on the track theme.

sessions.title: Running Software Factory Efficiently at Uber Scale: Holding Agent Spend Steady While Requests Grew 9X
sessions.abstract: Uber attributes 70%+ of PRs to coding agents, uses 5K+ agent skills and routes all MCP traffic through one gateway fronting 1,000+ servers. How it kept agent spend flat while requests grew 9x.

sessions.title: How Airbnb Guardrailed Its AI Customer Support Agent
sessions.abstract: The less-publicized guardrail layer behind Airbnb's AI support assistant: keeping an agent safe when it serves millions, carries multi-turn context and can trigger account actions.

sessions.title: LLM Flip-Flops: From Reliability Risk to a Hill-Climbing Signal
sessions.abstract: The same task run twice through the same LLM can give materially different answers. Treats that inconsistency as a real product risk, then shows how to use it as a signal for improving the system.

sessions.title: Unconference: Guardrails & Safety Nets
sessions.abstract: Open-space discussion on the track theme.

sessions.title: Agentic Trust: Securing AI Agents in Production
sessions.abstract: Practical steps to run an existing AI agent more securely in production today; deliberately out of scope: model training and alignment.

sessions.title: Testing & Verification for Code-Generating Agents
APIs That Can't Afford to Be Wrong: Lessons from Moving Money
sessions.abstract: Common API advice assumes cheap retries and a single source of truth; payments break both. Lessons from designing for card networks that demand an approve/decline in about three seconds.

sessions.title: Everything I Knew About Developer Experience Is Wrong for Agents
sessions.abstract: DX practices were learned from human users; agents are a different kind of consumer, and some accepted best practices actively work against them.

sessions.title: The Schema Was Never Enough: The World in Protocols
sessions.abstract: Auctions, double-entry bookkeeping and brokerage transfers are protocols, and so are APIs. Protocols reduce ambiguity, but the world stays messy; what that means for API design.

sessions.title: No New Backend: The API Layer Behind 800+ Agent-Built Apps at Duolingo
sessions.abstract: Duolingo's BuildingHub lets any employee describe an internal tool and get a working app wired to company systems (350 employees have built one). The API layer that makes it work.

sessions.title: Unconference: Modern API Design
sessions.abstract: Open-space discussion on the track theme.

sessions.title: Stop Fighting the Remodel: API Design for Models That Outgrew Their Boundaries
sessions.abstract: Netflix's core domain models strained as Ads, Games, Live and new content types pulled entities in different directions. How to design APIs for models that outgrew their original boundaries.

sessions.title: The Freeze Paradox: Why Stopping Deployments Doesn't Stop Failures
sessions.abstract: Teams often react to failure by freezing deploys. Examines, from Netflix experience, why halting change doesn't actually stop failures in complex systems.

sessions.title: Adapt or Drift: Resilience Engineering When AI Moves the Operating Point
sessions.abstract: Resilience requires adaptation, but adaptation is risky: under sustained (AI-driven) pressure, systems and orgs can drift toward failure while still looking healthy.

sessions.title: Unconference: Resilience Engineering
sessions.abstract: Open-space discussion on the track theme.

sessions.title: Saturation: How Your Software Will Fail at Scale
sessions.abstract: Every system has limits; what happens when it hits one. A look at saturation as a failure mode and how to reason about it.

sessions.title: What Is Incident Severity, but a Lie Agreed Upon?
sessions.abstract: Are severity levels clearly defined, argued over mid-incident, or even used? Questions how orgs pick and distinguish incident severities.

sessions.title: It's Never the Thing That Broke: Learning From Incidents at (AI) Speed
sessions.abstract: Incidents come from many normal changes interacting, not one broken part. How to keep learning from incidents when AI accelerates change.

sessions.title: Legacy vs. AI-Native Is the Wrong Question: Architecting the Modern Platform
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Freshworks). Leaders modernizing operational platforms are told to choose stable enterprise software or fast AI-native tools; argues that's a false binary.

sessions.title: Beyond the Model: Engineering the Agent Harness for Autonomous Software Delivery
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (IBM). Code generation is no longer the hard part; orchestrating agents so output is verifiable, governed and repeatable is, and the surrounding harness usually limits results more than the model.

sessions.title: Your Agents Lack Context: Here's How to Fix 'You're absolutely right!'
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Unblocked). AI coding tools write code, but rarely code that fits your org, because they lack organizational context; how to supply it.

sessions.title: Wait, You're Still Doing PRs?
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Atomic). PRs were built for outside contributors and maintainers to shape a change together; asks whether that model still fits agent-driven development.

sessions.title: AI Amplifies Everything, Including Your Mess: Lessons from Delivering with AI at Global Scale
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Nu). AI magnifies a team's existing habits. Lessons from rebuilding an SDLC around AI while shipping Nu Global, a crypto-rails financial platform.

sessions.title: Apache Spark: Structured Streaming Real-Time Mode
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Databricks). Structured Streaming suits seconds-to-minutes ETL but couldn't serve millisecond use cases; introduces its real-time mode.

sessions.title: Model-Harness Co-Training: Data-Driven Optimization Toward Pareto-Optimal Agents
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Lucidic AI). Teams tune either the harness or the model, but the two are interdependent; argues for optimizing them jointly using data.

sessions.title: Why Optimized Application Infrastructure (not just GPUs and LLMs) Can Scale Your AI Investments
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Azul). AI production costs outrun pilots while attention goes to GPUs and models; argues the Java/streaming/data runtime underneath is where cost and performance can be won without re-architecture.

sessions.title: Building a Safe Software Factory
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Sonar). Agents made code cheap, so change volume has outgrown human review; how to build an automated software factory that stays safe.

sessions.title: The Context Gap: Why Correct Agents Fail
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Tacnode). Agents can each make valid edits that merge cleanly yet break the program; collisions happen in meaning, not text, which matters for semantic business decisions.

sessions.title: Engineering the Critical Path: Nine Reliability Patterns from Processing 350 Million Payments a Day
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Juspay). A few core mechanisms (failover, routing, release gates) decide whether a local fault becomes an outage; nine patterns for protecting them, from a 350M-payments/day system.

sessions.title: Sponsored session (details coming soon)
sessions.abstract: Sponsored session; details not yet published.

sessions.title: Orderly Keys, Wild Values: Adaptive Compression for Distributed Key-Value Storage
sessions.abstract: At Netflix scale (billions of requests, petabytes of KV data) small storage/network inefficiencies get expensive; adaptive compression techniques for distributed key-value storage.

sessions.title: How to Build Online Systems with Object Storage
sessions.abstract: 'Diskless' systems that delegate durability to object storage are now common; why, and how to build latency-sensitive online systems on top of it.

sessions.title: Autoscaling 800 Valkey Clusters: Distributed Systems Lessons from Scaling Stateful Fleets
sessions.abstract: Resizing a sharded datastore means moving key-range ownership under live traffic, too slow to react to spikes. Lessons from autoscaling ~800 Valkey clusters at Snap.

sessions.title: Unconference: Distributed Systems in Production
sessions.abstract: Open-space discussion on the track theme.

sessions.title: When Your Users Are Agents: Lessons from a Distributed Postgres Platform
sessions.abstract: Distributed systems assume sane connection lifetimes, retries that stop and predictable queries. What breaks when AI agents become the main users of a distributed Postgres platform.

sessions.title: Adaptive Systems in Production: What Recommendation Systems Can Teach Us About Agents
sessions.abstract: Agent problems like uncertain evaluation, feedback loops and behavioral drift are well known from recommender systems; applies those lessons to agents.

sessions.title: Skills, Memory, or Fine-Tuning? The Engineering Loop Behind Production Agents
sessions.abstract: Patterns from improving hundreds of production agents serving millions of requests: when skills, memory or fine-tuning actually make an agent better after launch.

sessions.title: Inside Asimov: BlackRock's Platform Architecture for Applied AI at Scale
sessions.abstract: BlackRock's Portfolio Management Group pairs investment expertise with shared AI capabilities to change research; the platform architecture (Asimov) behind it.

sessions.title: The Revenge of the Data Scientist: Why Reliable AI Needs Evals, Traces, and Metrics
sessions.abstract: Prototyping on foundation-model APIs is easy; knowing whether it works with real users and messy data is not. Argues reliability comes from data-science fundamentals: evals, traces, metrics.

sessions.title: Lessons from Building a $100M Product in Six Weeks at OpenAI
sessions.abstract: Engineering is moving from line-by-line coding to an async model where agents execute, verify and retry while humans own intent, architecture, constraints and release calls; lessons from a fast OpenAI launch.

sessions.title: Bridging Retrieval and Ranking: From LLM Embeddings and Graph Features to a GPU-Served DLRM
sessions.abstract: LinkedIn Feed retrieval picks posts from hundreds of millions of candidates in ~120 ms; the path from LLM embeddings and graph features to a GPU-served ranking model.

sessions.title: Failing in Layers: Lessons from Rebuilding Netflix's ML Serving Platform
sessions.abstract: What goes wrong when a model must serve real traffic reliably, and why Netflix's rebuilt ML serving system ended up shaped the way it is.

sessions.title: Nobody Knows Everything (and That's OK): Building Alignment in Complex, Rapidly Changing Environments
sessions.abstract: How Staff+ engineers build alignment across org and technical boundaries, including in areas where they aren't the deepest expert.

sessions.title: Use AI to Multiply Your Team as a Staff Engineer
sessions.abstract: Most AI-for-engineers advice is about individual speed, which is IC work. What a staff engineer's job becomes when AI raises everyone's baseline, and where leverage now comes from.

sessions.title: Scaling Tech by Aligning Humans
sessions.abstract: Without a north star and shared technical strategy, separate product strategies create disconnected solutions and tech debt; aligning people to scale technology.

sessions.title: Transitioning From a Startup to a Mature Platform
sessions.abstract: How needs shift from zero customers to thousands, and the resulting changes in code, architecture, organization and mindset.

sessions.title: Learning What's Already There: A Breadth-Based Approach To Onboarding
sessions.abstract: A breadth-first way to quickly build your network and context when joining a new organization.

sessions.title: Unconference: Staff+ Engineering Skills
sessions.abstract: Open-space discussion on the track theme.

sessions.title: Breaking Down the Walls to Python & Big Data + AI Performance with Transpilation and LLMs
sessions.abstract: PySpark's slow Python UDFs frustrate many users; explores using transpilation and LLMs to close the performance gap.

sessions.title: Building a Data Platform with AI
sessions.abstract: A data platform is where infrastructure, governance, operations and user experience meet; using AI to build and evolve one (OpenAI data infra perspective).

sessions.title: One Does Not Simply Add Synchronous Writes - Bridging Batch and Real Time with Apache Iceberg
sessions.abstract: Datadog Reference Tables were built for big async uploads; customers wanted synchronous row-level edits. How the team added them on Apache Iceberg without losing batch scale.

sessions.title: Building a StreamHouse: Turning Kafka Streams into a Millisecond Query Layer
sessions.abstract: Pairing Kafka with Flink materialized views to build a low-latency serving layer (Lightning Tables): Kafka as source of truth, hot/warm/historical tiers, trade-offs and failure modes.

sessions.title: From Datasets to Data Products: Powering Trusted AI for Social Impact
sessions.abstract: An agent acting for a nonprofit is only as trustworthy as its data; how Blackbaud turns scattered datasets into data products for trusted AI.

sessions.title: Iceberg V4: The Next Chapter in Table Formats
sessions.abstract: With Iceberg V3 adoption growing, the planned scope and priorities of the V4 spec and the status of open proposals.

sessions.title: Feeling Faster Isn't a Metric: Measuring AI's Real Engineering Impact
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (GitKraken). A 2026 survey of 554 developers and leaders: AI tools are near-universal and feel faster, but few teams can actually quantify the impact; how to measure it.

sessions.title: Notes From 300 Installs Inside Someone Else's Cloud
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Groundcover). Running a storage/query backend inside customers' VPCs (they own infra, vendor runs ops): what went wrong across hundreds of Kubernetes installs.

sessions.title: Why Your Document AI Fails in Production — And How to Fix the Infrastructure Underneath It
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Nutrient). Document AI that demos well breaks in production: lost structure at ingestion, rendering edge cases, inconsistent extraction, plus governance when agents make decisions.

sessions.title: Trust, but Verify: Delivering Quality with Agentic Workflows
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Antithesis). Agent unreliability and review overload aren't new: humans were always error-prone. Focus on verifying what ships rather than assuming correctness.

sessions.title: Your Agents Have Amnesia: Lessons from Building a Memory Layer for Multi-Agent Systems
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (YugabyteDB). Agents pass only final outputs, so reasoning and failed attempts are lost; lessons from building a shared memory layer for multi-agent systems.

sessions.title: Sponsored session (details coming soon)
sessions.abstract: Sponsored session; details not yet published.

sessions.title: You Steer, Agents Execute: Developer-Led Modernization with Agentic AI
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (IBM). Legacy modernization stalls on hidden dependencies and a false choice between leaving systems alone or rewriting; a developer-steered, agent-executed middle path.

sessions.title: Architecting Security into the Agentic SDLC
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Endor Labs). As agents write more code, securing it needs AI-driven security built into the SDLC by design.

sessions.title: Drawing the Rest of the Owl: A Blueprint for Your Software Factory
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Harness). Between 'software factories mean slop and incidents' and 'they're the future', a practical blueprint for building one.

sessions.title: Sponsored session (details coming soon)
sessions.abstract: Sponsored session; details not yet published.

sessions.title: Code is abundant, Confidence is Scarce: What 1K Devs Say about Coding with Agents
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Sonar). Survey of ~1,000 developers: about two-thirds of committed code is now AI-generated or assisted, and many expect autonomous software factories soon; the confidence gap.

sessions.title: Sponsored session (details coming soon)
sessions.abstract: Sponsored session; details not yet published.

sessions.title: How Netflix Retrofitted Its SDLC for AI Coding Agents
sessions.abstract: Coding agents mirror what a codebase already contains and guess at what isn't written down; how Netflix reshaped its SDLC so agents follow team standards by default.

sessions.title: Making Production Legible to Agents: Lessons From Building an Observability MCP
sessions.abstract: Agents that can query production telemetry test hypotheses instead of guessing; 40%+ of Honeycomb weekly users query via its MCP. Why an MCP must be more than an API wrapper: token efficiency, tool descriptions, schemas, evals.

sessions.title: Efficient GPU Agents: Infra for Autonomous LLM Perf Optimization
sessions.abstract: Parasail's agent platform for LLM serving performance work on Kubernetes GPU clusters: scheduling GPU experiments, mirroring production traffic for fair benchmarks, canary-gated rollouts with human oversight.

sessions.title: Dreams on Paper: How Agents Learn from Experience
sessions.abstract: Agents leave detailed traces, but traces aren't memory; three primitives for turning session history into knowledge an agent can act on.

sessions.title: Avoiding Prompt Debt & Other Context Failures
sessions.abstract: Agent prompts accrete one-line hotfixes and escalating instructions until they're brittle and overfit to aging models; how to avoid prompt debt and related context failures.

sessions.title: Features With Futures
sessions.abstract: Software is worth what it does now plus the options it keeps open. What if AI-assisted development invested in both, and what happens when teams measure only shipped features?

sessions.title: No More Small Systems, How AI May Bring Large System Problems to Everyone
sessions.abstract: AI-boosted productivity brings new problems, some LLM-specific but many simply from producing far more stuff; large-system problems arriving at every organization.

sessions.title: Growing Engineers in the Era of Agentic Coding
sessions.abstract: Early-career engineers now work through an agent rather than directly in a codebase; this changes how they learn but doesn't fundamentally break how they grow.

sessions.title: Shipping Faster, Understanding Less
sessions.abstract: AI speeds development faster than practices adapt; three linked threats to software health: technical debt, cognitive debt and intent debt.

sessions.title: The Diary of an AI Adopter: How I Went From Skeptical to Enthusiastic in Our Organization's AI Migration Efforts
sessions.abstract: Amid mixed market results, AI-linked layoffs and rollbacks over cost, one leader's path from skeptic to enthusiast and what successful enterprise AI adoption looks like.

sessions.title: Platform Engineering's Second Act: From Vending Machine to Passport Control
sessions.abstract: Revisits a QCon SF talk from three years ago on acceleration, autonomy and accountability as platform pillars; how AI changes what each requires and the platform team's job.

sessions.title: Beyond the Kubernetes API: Building LinkedIn's Compute Platform
sessions.abstract: LinkedIn runs Kubernetes on 500K+ bare-metal machines and 5M pods with 110K+ deploys a week, exposing curated platform offerings instead of raw Kubernetes.

sessions.title: Observability: The Missing Control Plane for Agentic Engineering
sessions.abstract: As agents test, deploy and operate software, the key question is what they may decide without a human; observability as the control plane that answers it.

sessions.title: Why Most Platform Teams Fail: The Adoption Problem Nobody Wants to Own
sessions.abstract: Polished platforms launch and teams keep working the old way because adoption was assumed, not owned; who should own driving adoption.

sessions.title: Building a Migration Platform: Moving 100+ Netflix RDBMS Workloads to Aurora PostgreSQL
sessions.abstract: After Netflix chose (late 2024) to consolidate most relational use cases on Aurora PostgreSQL, the migration platform built to move 100+ workloads.

sessions.title: Builder-Driven Development: Rebuilding the Organization Around the Builder
sessions.abstract: Managing agent development like classic projects (upfront requirements, closing demo) fails because the best insights emerge outside planning docs; reorganizing around the builder.

sessions.title: Legacy as Leverage: How Brownfield Work Builds Technical Judgment
sessions.abstract: Legacy work is often treated as a chore before 'real' projects; reframes brownfield work as a primary source of technical judgment.

sessions.title: Product Engineering: When code costs nothing, what's next?
sessions.abstract: Agents produce far more code but only a little more ships, because human review is the bottleneck; guidance for engineering leaders on that gap.

sessions.title: You Can't Read the Code Anymore - Verifying Software in the Age of AI
sessions.abstract: With AI writing most code, the hard part becomes verification, a weaker team skill; ship pressure pushes toward skimmed diffs and light QA instead of rigorous checks.

sessions.title: When Everyone Can Code, Who Owns Production?
sessions.abstract: AI makes writing code easy, but every change must still be deployed, observed, operated, debugged and kept reliable; who owns production when everyone codes.

sessions.title: Simulating the Universe, 100 Times Over: Engineering Highly-Concurrent Agent Testing
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Lucidic AI). Agent testing is hard: live data shifts, static datasets go stale and testing on real systems is risky and irreproducible; simulating environments at high concurrency.

sessions.title: The Men in Black Know What's in Your JavaScript and How to Fix it!
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (TuxCare). What's really hiding in node_modules, and why knowing exactly what you ship matters as supply-chain attacks rise.

sessions.title: The Fast, The Furious and The Fatigued
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Harness). Survey of 700+ engineering leaders: high deploy frequency can mask off-hours firefighting, instability and burnout; automated governance, verification and progressive delivery as the fix.

sessions.title: Multi-Agent Coding with Omnigent
sessions.abstract: Sponsored (Databricks). Developers juggle several coding agents in separate tools with no shared context; Omnigent as a meta-harness that coordinates them.

sessions.title: The InfoQ Certified Architect Program at QCon San Francisco
sessions.abstract: Cohort program for senior engineers/architects spanning the conference (reflection sessions, cohort lunch, networking), capped by a half-day workshop on participants' own challenges; leads to the ICSAET credential.

sessions.title: Building AI Agents: A Practical Framework for Choosing the Right SDK
sessions.abstract: Half-day. The agent SDK landscape is crowded; a framework for evaluating and choosing an SDK against your requirements.

sessions.title: [SOLD OUT] The Human Architecture Problem: Designing Teams That Scale With AI [Half-day version]
sessions.abstract: Half-day (sold out). AI-driven orgs are limited more by team structure, decision rights and trust than by tools; designing teams where humans and AI work well together.

sessions.title: AI for Java Developers
sessions.abstract: Half-day, beginner-intermediate. Java developers don't need to switch to Python to build with AI; hands-on AI development from the Java/Spring side.

sessions.title: Measuring What Matters: Building a Developer Productivity Program Engineers Can Trust
sessions.abstract: Half-day workshop. Build a dev productivity program on meaningful signals: pairing metrics with tension metrics, mixing quantitative and qualitative data, tying results to outcomes including AI ROI.

sessions.title: Supercharge Your Work With Claude Code and Codex
sessions.abstract: Half-day for developers already using coding agents: getting more from Claude Code and Codex for Q&A, docs, debugging, small changes and code review.

sessions.title: How To Write Skills That Actually Work
sessions.abstract: Half-day. Why some agent skills work and others silently fail or get misfired, and how to measure what each skill adds before improving it.

sessions.title: Psychological Safety as Infrastructure: Building Teams That Fail Fast With AI
sessions.abstract: Half-day. AI adoption stalls when people don't feel safe to experiment, report errors or voice distrust of AI output; building that safety into how teams operate.

sessions.title: AI-Assisted Coding Master Class: Build Your Mission Control
sessions.abstract: Half-day. Most engineers under-invest in their environment setup; configuring a 'mission control' to get much more out of AI coding agents.

sessions.title: The Fundamentals of Software Engineering in the Age of AI
sessions.abstract: Half-day. Every tooling wave (codegen, low-code, no-code) was said to end software engineering; the role adapts, fundamentals persist, and engineers who know the craft benefit most.

sessions.title: The Incident Lab: Responding to and Learning From Production Failures
sessions.abstract: Full-day, hands-on. For orgs that have alerting, runbooks, on-call and reviews yet repeat the same failures: practicing incident response and extracting real learning.

sessions.title: The Human Architecture Problem: Designing Teams That Scale With AI [Full-Day Version]
sessions.abstract: Full-day version: team structures, decision rights and trust determine whether humans and AI collaborate well; deeper work on designing for it.

sessions.title: Effective AI-Native Development with Harness Engineering
sessions.abstract: Full-day. AI coding demos use greenfield repos; real work is long-lived code with thin tests and legacy frameworks. Applying harness engineering to AI-native development there.

sessions.title: Agent MCP Workshop: Building Your Own Java-Based MCP Server
sessions.abstract: Full-day, intermediate, instructor-led: build a Model Context Protocol server in Java from scratch.

speakers.bio_short: Business psychologist and coach with 16+ years helping tech leaders and teams; co-founded Bravely (training/coaching for tech) and has worked with 50+ startups and scaleups.

speakers.name: Plum Ertz
speakers.title: Senior Director, Engineering
speakers.bio_short: Engineering leader focused on accessibility, UI development and scaling systems and teams; background in marketing, media and fintech, now leading engineering for accessible direct-to-patient care at Ro.

speakers.name: Jacob Murphy
speakers.title: Staff Software Engineer; Valkey maintainer & TSC member
speakers.bio_short: Valkey maintainer and Technical Steering Committee member who sets technical direction for Google's managed Redis/Valkey/Memcached; focuses on distributed systems, HA and cache scaling.

speakers.name: Cat Swetel
speakers.bio_short: Listed on the Nubank session page only; no title, company or bio shown, and not on the speakers index.

speakers.name: Nancy Zheng
speakers.title: VP of Engineering, AI Inference
